symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the source vector, the length of the transform on the source grid.
symbols.quote: The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the target vector, the length of the transform on the target grid.
symbols.quote: The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

symbols.name: relative excess
symbols.meaning: The ratio t/s minus one, measuring how much longer the target is than the source.
symbols.quote: Let $\theta=t/s-1$ be the relative excess of $t$ over $s$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: An integer, at least 2, that sets the width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: The identity needs $\theta>p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha\ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

symbols.name: precision
symbols.meaning: The integer precision of the numerical approximation, which bounds how large theta must be.
symbols.quote: The identity needs $\theta>p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha\ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of length-s vectors sending u to the vector with entries u_{tj} at index j, indices taken modulo s.
symbols.quote: The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices, with subscripts taken modulo the length:

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of length-t vectors sending v to the vector with entries v_{-sk} at index k, indices taken modulo t.
symbols.quote: The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices, with subscripts taken modulo the length:

symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized transform of length s, the transform F_q with q equal to s.
symbols.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for the normalized transforms of length $s$ and $t$, that is, $F_q$ with $q=s$ or $q=t$.

symbols.name: target transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized transform of length t, the transform F_q with q equal to t.
symbols.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for the normalized transforms of length $s$ and $t$, that is, $F_q$ with $q=s$ or $q=t$.

symbols.name: source-to-target Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian map sending length-s vectors to length-t vectors, with entries (Su)_k given by a Gaussian-weighted sum over j.
symbols.quote: The two Gaussian maps $S$ and $T$ are built from the [Gaussian function](gaussian-function.md).

symbols.name: target-to-source Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian map sending length-s vectors to length-t vectors, with entries (Tu)_k given by a second Gaussian-weighted sum over j.
symbols.quote: The two Gaussian maps $S$ and $T$ are built from the [Gaussian function](gaussian-function.md).

symbols.name: nearest target index
symbols.meaning: For each source position j, the integer nearest to tj/s, which is the target entry that C selects.
symbols.quote: $C$ maps length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors by taking, for each $j$ with $0\le j<s$, the entry at $\mu_j$, the integer nearest to $tj/s$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map from length-t vectors to length-s vectors that copies the entries at the indices mu_j.
symbols.quote: $C$ maps length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors by taking, for each $j$ with $0\le j<s$, the entry at $\mu_j$, the integer nearest to $tj/s$.

symbols.name: diagonal correction
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map on length-s vectors whose j-th factor cancels the Gaussian factor of T at entry mu_j.
symbols.quote: The diagonal map $D$ is $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2(tj/s-\mu_j)^2}u_j$ on length-$s$ vectors, which cancels the Gaussian factor of $T$ at that entry.

symbols.name: correction map
symbols.meaning: The map CTD on length-s vectors, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Put $N=CTD$.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The map that leaves every vector unchanged.
symbols.quote: Its $j$th entry is $u_j$ plus other terms, so $N$ is close to $I$, the identity map, which leaves every vector unchanged.

symbols.name: series index
symbols.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series, a non-negative integer.

symbols.name: scaled diagonal map
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map D multiplied by the scalar 2 to the power minus (2 alpha squared minus 2).
symbols.quote: Write $D'=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}D$ for the scaled diagonal map.

symbols.name: source-to-target contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction S/2, mapping length-s vectors to length-t vectors.
symbols.quote: $A$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors, and $B_0$ maps them back, where $A=S/2$ and $B_0=D'N^{-1}C/2$.

symbols.name: target-to-source contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction D' N^{-1} C / 2, mapping length-t vectors back to length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: $A$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors, and $B_0$ maps them back, where $A=S/2$ and $B_0=D'N^{-1}C/2$.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling is an identity that replaces the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of an arbitrary length by transforms whose lengths are powers of two.
It serves the [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of digit vectors, which needs such transforms.
The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.
The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices, with subscripts taken modulo the length:
The size of $N-I$ is measured by its [operator norm](operator-norm.md), $\|N-I\|$.
The two Gaussian maps $S$ and $T$ are built from the [Gaussian function](gaussian-function.md).
